title: Volume 5 — the first photograph: vendor OVMF vs coreboot, same machine (QEMU q35), zero hardware touched

method.instrument: fw.spi.map via `omarchy-firmware spi-map --dump <image>` — the offline dump_path seam, read-only, stdlib parse (FVs, FFS, descriptor, Boot Guard manifests)
method.coreboot_layer: cbfstool print (built from coreboot-25.12) — coreboot does not use the PI/FFS container, so the vendor instrument correctly reports zero FVs; the CBFS layer is the coreboot-native equivalent inventory
method.vendor_depth: cross-cited from lab/ovmf-census.json (rings 1-8) on byte-identical images (sha256 match)
honesty: offline image analysis — no chip was read or written; +0 octet holds
OVMF_CODE_4M*.fd are the CODE-only halves of a 4 MiB split (CODE+VARS); the NV varstore lives in OVMF_VARS_4M.fd, not in the photographed image

the vendor instrument's outer-layer scan shows 6 FFS files on OVMF because the DXE FV is nested inside an FFS file; the census pierced that nesting (135/144 files) — both numbers are labelled, not contradictory
no flash descriptor on any image: the OVMF .fd files are partial regions, coreboot.rom is a descriptorless QEMU image — on real boards the descriptor/IFD layout will differ

spi_map.boot_guard: no Intel Boot Guard manifests — expected on AMD boards (the PSP signs the AGESA blobs instead)
no Intel Boot Guard manifests — expected on AMD boards (the PSP signs the AGESA blobs instead)
no Intel Boot Guard manifests — expected on AMD boards (the PSP signs the AGESA blobs instead)

the_delta: container: vendor OVMF is a PI firmware volume world (FFS2, nested FVs, 135-144 FFS files); coreboot is a CBFS world (flat named entries, 5 stages + payload + metadata) — the two firmwares do not share a container format

boot: vendor boots via DXE Core + 115 DXE drivers (plain) with an 8-module SMM island (secboot); coreboot boots via bootblock→romstage→ramstage→postcar→SeaBIOS payload — the 'payload' IS the architectural answer to what SMM/DXE used to be
NVRAM: vendor keeps variable stores in flash (OVMF_VARS_4M.fd, SECUREBOOT_CONFIGURATION etc. — ring 7); the coreboot q35 build carries cmos_layout.bin and no flash NV varstore

instruments: the repo's spi-map reads the vendor world natively and honestly reports zero FVs on coreboot — photographing a real coreboot board day-X will need a CBFS lens; that lens now exists in rehearsal form (cbfstool parse)
Boot Guard manifests: absent on all three images (QEMU) — the fused-vs-deactivated question stays hardware-only, unchanged from the doctrine
